entry.translit: hāʾōḇôṯ wᵉhayyiddᵉʿōnîm (sg. ʾôḇ; yiddᵉʿōnî) (8:19); kᵉʾôḇ mē-ʾereṣ (29:4)
entry.strongs: H178 (ʾôḇ); H3049 (yiddᵉʿōnî). Strong's numbers from model recall, not concordance-verified.
entry.lemma: ʾôḇ 'spirit of the dead; one who calls it up'; yiddᵉʿōnî 'knowing (spirit); one who consults it' (from ydʿ 'know')
entry.partOfSpeech: nouns (fem. pl. ʾōḇôṯ, masc. pl. yiddᵉʿōnîm), articular, as objects of dāraš ʾel 'seek, consult'
entry.literal: the ʾôḇ-spirits and the knowing ones
entry.standardEnglish: them that have familiar spirits and … the wizards (ASV, KJV); the ghosts and the familiar spirits (JPS 1917; NJPS 'the ghosts and familiar spirits'); NRSV 'the ghosts and the familiar spirits' (not verified)
entry.wohChoice: 'the ghosts and the familiar spirits' at 8:19 ('Seek the ghosts and the familiar spirits that chirp and mutter'): the pair rendered as the spirits consulted, not as the practitioners, because the following participles hamᵉṣap̄ṣᵉp̄îm wᵉhammahgîm describe their voices. Context rule for later sites of the pair in Isaiah (19:3): 'the ghosts' / 'the familiar spirits' where the consulted spirits are meant; 'mediums' / 'necromancers' only where the context requires persons, with a note. No etymological rendering ('the knowing ones') in the line. ʾôḇ alone in the simile kᵉʾôḇ mē-ʾereṣ at 29:4 is 'a ghost' ('your voice will be like that of a ghost from the ground'), governed by this entry (moved from ariel-ob-isaiah-29, founder ruling 2026-11-26); at 29:4 the verb ṣpṣp is rendered 'whisper' ('your speech will whisper'), where 8:19 has 'chirp' for its participle.
entry.rationale: ʾôḇ and yiddᵉʿōnî are the paired terms of the Hebrew Bible's necromancy vocabulary (Lev 19:31; 20:6, 27; Deut 18:11; 1 Sam 28:3, 9; 2 Kgs 21:6; 23:24; Isa 19:3). Both can denote either the spirit of the dead that is consulted or the person who consults it: Lev 20:27 speaks of a man or woman 'in whom is' an ʾôḇ or yiddᵉʿōnî, while 1 Sam 28:3 has Saul remove them from the land (BDB; HALOT; Tropper, DDD s.v. 'Spirit of the dead'; not verified). At Isa 8:19 the spirits are meant: the articular participles 'that chirp and that mutter' describe the faint voices of the dead, as the voice of the ghost 'chirps' (tᵉṣap̄ṣēp̄) from the dust at 29:4. JPS 1917 and NJPS (both verified on Sefaria) render 'the ghosts and the familiar spirits', and NRSV is reported to do the same; ASV's 'them that have familiar spirits … the wizards' renders practitioners and loses the link between the nouns and the participles. 'Ghost' also keeps 8:19 consistent with 29:4, where the overlay already renders ʾôḇ 'a ghost'. 'Familiar spirit' is kept for yiddᵉʿōnî because it is the established English term for this word in all three versions; the objection recorded at 29:4 (that the phrase suggests a witch's animal companion) was made against using it for ʾôḇ, and the pairing with 'ghosts' makes the sense plain here. No central entry covers either term (central v2.93.0 searched by id, source, wohChoice, rationale and appliesTo for Lev 19:31, 20:6, 27, Deut 18:11, 1 Sam 28, 2 Kgs 21:6, 23:24); the entry is placed in the overlay and should be promoted to central when Leviticus 19-20, Deuteronomy 18 or 1 Samuel 28 is translated. The rendering is the standard modern one and carries no lens, so the claim is direct. Housekeeping (founder ruling 2026-11-26): ISA-29:4 is moved here from ariel-ob-isaiah-29, which now governs only the Ariel sites (29:1, 2, 7), so that ʾôḇ 'ghost' is governed by one entry in the book. The reasons for 'a ghost' at 29:4 carry over: ASV's 'one that hath a familiar spirit' is an archaism that modern readers take to mean a witch's companion animal, and NRSV and NJPS have 'a ghost'. At 29:4 the line renders the verb ṣpṣp 'whisper' ('from the dust your speech will whisper'), while 8:19 has 'chirp' for the participle hamᵉṣap̄ṣᵉp̄îm; the two English verbs are not harmonised in this wave, and the difference is an open item for the next revision of either chapter.

entry.literal: with a stylus of a man; and he/it shall go up … his/its wings; shout (?) … be shattered; as with strength of the hand; attestation; for signs and for tokens; dawn; and he shall pass through it … and curse by his king; driven out; he made light … he made heavy
entry.standardEnglish: with the pen of a man / in common script; it … its (ASV) / he … his (KJV, JPS 1917); make an uproar (ASV) / band together (NJPS); with a strong hand (ASV) / took me by the hand (NJPS); testimony (ASV) / message (NJPS); signs and wonders (ASV) / signs and portents (NJPS); morning (ASV) / dawn (NJPS); they … their (ASV) / he … his (NJPS); driven away (ASV); made glorious (ASV) / dealt a more grievous blow (JPS 1917)
entry.wohChoice: 8:1 'a large tablet … with the pen of a man' (ASV literal; 'in common script' in commentary); 8:7-8 masculine pronouns kept as 'he … his' (KJV, JPS 1917; River or king left open), kᵉḇôḏô 'his glory' under the wave concordance; 8:9 rōʿû 'Make an uproar' (rwʿ), wāḥōttû 'be shattered', merḥaqqê-ʾāreṣ under eretz-cosmic-scope-isaiah-24; 8:11 'with a strong hand, and instructed me' (MT ysr); 8:16, 20 tᵉʿûḏāh 'testimony' in both verses, tôrāh 'teaching' under torah-teaching-isaiah, 8:16 the imperatives are the prophet's, because the line closes YHWH's speech at the end of 8:15 (house style lower-cases divine pronouns, so 'my disciples' does not itself decide the speaker); 8:18 'for signs and for wonders' (as Deut 4:34 in the project's Torah; portent sense in commentary); 8:20 'To the teaching and to the testimony!' as exclamation, šaḥar 'dawn'; 8:21 plural 'they … their' for the singular collective, qillēl bᵉ- 'curse by'; 8:22 'into thick darkness they shall be driven away' (mᵉnuddāḥ Pual participle); 8:23 'In the former time he brought into contempt … but in the latter time he has made it glorious' (ASV reversal reading). 8:19b-21 construal (A), the prophet's reply, is kept (founder ruling 2026-11-26); the continued quotation of JPS 1917 and NJPS, with ʾĕlōhîm as the dead (NJPS 'its divine beings'), is reported in commentary at 8:19-21 and not printed.
entry.rationale: Each item is a site where the Translator flagged a choice between the ASV rendering and a defensible alternative. The Editor keeps the established sense of the Masoretic Text in every case and records the alternatives in commentary; no item adopts an emendation and none carries a project reading. The checks are these: ASV 1901 was verified against its text (it has 'it … its' at 8:7-8, not 'he … his' as the draft reported, so the line's 'he … his' rests on KJV and JPS 1917, both verified, and leaves the River/king referent open as the Hebrew masculine does); JPS 1917 and NJPS were verified on Sefaria, including NJPS 'Band together' (8:9), 'took me by the hand' (8:11), 'message' (8:16), 'signs and portents' (8:18) and the persons reading of 8:23, and JPS 1917's judgment reading of hiḵbîḏ at 8:23 ('dealt a more grievous blow'), a construal discussed in Emerton, JSS 14 (1969) 151-175 (bibliographic details verified via Crossref; his conclusion not checked). 'Signs and wonders' is kept at 8:18, against NJPS 'portents', because the project renders the same pair 'signs … wonders' at Deut 4:34 and the pair should stay recognisable across the corpus; the sense of môp̄ēṯ as an ominous token is explained in commentary. 'Testimony' is kept for tᵉʿûḏāh at both 8:16 and 8:20 so that the repeated pair is visible. At 8:23 the reversal reading (contempt, then glory) is kept because it is the standard construal of hēqal/hiḵbîḏ in the major English versions and lexica (BDB kbd Hiphil 'make honourable'; not verified); its reuse at Matt 4:15-16 is noted in commentary and is not the reason for the choice. The kāḇôḏ of 8:7 is the Assyrian king's array, so the divine-glory entries are not applied; 'glory' follows the wave concordance. The entry may be folded into a wave-level crux entry at merge. Post-review (wave I-3 Reviewer): the 8:20 exclamation item goes with construal (A) of 8:19, which rests on ASV and KJV and was confirmed by founder ruling 2026-11-26; JPS 1917 and NJPS both continue the quotation through 8:20a, and that reading is reported in commentary.
